q: 1. Mechanical lines are types of
options: line of drawn with free hand
explain: Mechanical lines refer to precise lines created using instruments like scales and T-squares rather than free-hand sketching.

q: 2. Drawing pins/cello tapes are used to .............
explain: Drawing pins and cello tape are used to fix (secure) the drawing sheet firmly onto the drawing board so it does not shift while drawing.

q: 3. The letter 'H' labeled in a drawing pencil indicates .............
explain: The 'H' grading on pencils denotes relative hardness of the graphite lead — a higher number before H (e.g., 4H) means a harder, lighter lead, useful for fine, thin lines.

q: 4. The latter 'H' labeled in a Drawing Pencil indicates
explain: The 'H' grading on a pencil denotes the relative hardness of its lead.

q: 5. Circles of small radii are drawn by means of a .............
explain: A bow compass, with its fine adjustment screw, is specifically designed for drawing small circles and arcs with high precision.

q: 6. In Engineering Drawing, French curves mean
options: drafting tools used to draw non-linear drawings
drafting tools used to draw oblong figures
explain: French curves are drafting templates of varying curvature used to draw smooth non-linear (irregular curved) lines.

q: 7. The following instrument is not used for drawing straight line .............
explain: Note: per the answer key, 'straight edge' is marked as not used for drawing straight lines in this context; set-squares and the board's working edge are the standard tools/guides actually used for ruling straight lines.

q: 8. Drawing board is made of .............
explain: Drawing boards are made of well-seasoned soft wood, which is light, easy to pin into, and resistant to warping when properly seasoned.

q: 9. During drawing stock of T-square is placed .............
options: adjoining the working edge of the board
adjoining the sliding edge of the board
explain: The stock (head) of the T-square is kept pressed against the working edge of the drawing board, allowing the blade to slide up and down accurately.

q: 10. The letter 'H' labeled in a Drawing pencil indicates
explain: The 'H' grade on a pencil lead denotes its relative hardness.

q: 11. Clinograph is a type of:
explain: A clinograph is an adjustable set square whose angle can be varied for drawing lines at any required inclination.

q: 12. French curve is used to draw
explain: French curves are templates for non-circular, mathematically irregular curves like ellipses or parabolas.

q: 13. The drawing prepared by a pencil and without use of drawing instrument is called
explain: Freehand sketching relies solely on the artist's eye and hand coordination without tools like rulers or compasses.

q: 14. Hard pencils are best used in .............
explain: Hard pencils (higher H grade) produce fine, precise, light lines, making them well suited to landscape/detail drawings requiring delicate line work, as per this reference's classification.

q: 15. The needle point of the compass should be ............. the lead point.
explain: For accurate circle drawing, the compass's needle (steel) point should be slightly shorter than the pencil/lead point so the pencil tip touches the paper properly while the needle anchors the center.

q: 16. *In Engineering Drawing, French Curves mean :
options: drafting tools used to draw non-linear figures
drafting tools used to draw oblong figures
explain: French curves are plastic or wooden templates used in manual drafting to draw smooth, non-circular curves that cannot be drawn with a compass.

q: 17. The drafting tool used to prepare a smooth curve line is called
explain: French curves are shaped templates specifically designed for drawing smooth curves that are not circular arcs.

q: 18. The letter 'H' labelled in a Drawing Pencil indicates -
explain: In pencil grading, 'H' stands for 'Hard,' indicating the relative hardness of the graphite lead; higher numbers mean harder leads.

q: 19. For drawing mechanical curves other than circles or circular arcs
explain: Non-circular mechanical curves (ellipses, involutes, spirals, etc.) are drawn using French curve templates.

q: 20. The most of the texture can be drawn with the help of drawing pen with line thickness
explain: For detailed texture and hatching, a specific medium-thick pen like 0.8mm is often used for emphasis.

q: 21. Eraser shield is best used in .............
explain: An eraser shield, which protects surrounding lines while erasing a specific area, is especially useful in detailed hand-drawn perspective drawings where selective correction is often needed without disturbing adjacent linework.

q: 22. Eraser shield is best used in
explain: An eraser shield protects adjacent lines while correcting errors, making it most useful for precise hand-drawn working drawings.

q: 23. A letter B in any pencil denotes
explain: In pencil grading, 'B' indicates a softer, darker lead, as opposed to 'H' which indicates hardness.

q: 24. Pencil drawings are generally corrected or revised with the help of :
explain: An eraser shield is a thin metal or plastic template that allows a drafter to erase small areas without disturbing the surrounding lines.

q: 25. Graphos are:
explain: Graphos is a technical pen used for drawing and writing (lettering) with interchangeable nibs.

q: 26. Templates are used for:
explain: Drafting templates have cut-out shapes for both regular curves/circles and standard geometric areas, speeding up repetitive drawing tasks.

q: 27. The hardness of pencil lead increases as numeral letter H
explain: A higher number preceding 'H' (e.g. 6H vs 2H) indicates progressively harder, lighter-marking lead.
A graphos is a type of pen with an interchangeable metal nib used for both drawing and lettering (writing) on technical drawings, making it a drawing-and-writing instrument.

q: 29. For drawing large size circle is drawn by.....
explain: A lengthening bar attaches to a compass to extend its reach for drawing large circles.

q: 30. To draw or measure angle is used by.....
explain: A protractor is the instrument specifically designed and graduated for drawing and measuring angles.

q: 31. Unnecessary lines is removed by .....
explain: An eraser is the standard tool used to remove unwanted or incorrect pencil lines from a drawing.

q: 32. What is used for drawing curves which can not drawn by compass
explain: French curves are used to draw smooth irregular curves that cannot be produced with a compass.

q: 33. T square is used to draw .............
explain: The T-square's blade slides along the board's working edge, making it primarily suited for drawing horizontal lines (vertical and inclined lines require set squares used in conjunction with it).

q: 34. The equipment used to draft vertical and angular line is .............
explain: Vertical and angular (inclined) lines are drawn using a set square placed against the T-square's blade, combining both tools together.

q: 35. The artificial light on the drawing board should be diffused light from .............
explain: Artificial lighting for a (typically right-handed) drafter should be diffused and directed from the left, avoiding shadows cast by the drafting hand and instruments over the work area.

q: 36. Which of the following is not a drawing hand tool?
explain: An alidade is a surveying sighting instrument, not a basic hand tool for drafting like a straight edge, French curve, or set square.

q: 37. Set squares are not used to draw .............
explain: Set squares, being rigid straight-edged triangles, cannot be used to draw irregular curves, which require a flexible tool like a French curve.

q: 38. Templates are used for .............
explain: Drafting templates (plastic sheets with cut-out shapes) are used to quickly and accurately trace irregular curves, standard symbols, and commonly repeated shapes on a drawing.

q: 39. Uses of the T-square, set squares, scale and protractor are combined in the .............
explain: A drafting machine integrates the functions of the T-square, set squares, scale, and protractor into a single adjustable device mounted on the drawing board.

q: 40. Circle and arcs are drawn by means of a .............
explain: A compass, with its adjustable pivot and pencil/pen leg, is the standard instrument used to draw circles and arcs of a given radius.

q: 41. Measurements from scale to the drawing are transferred with the aid of .............
explain: A divider, having two pointed legs, is used to transfer measured lengths directly from a scale onto the drawing without marking the scale itself.

q: 42. Clinograph is a type of .............
explain: A clinograph is an adjustable set square whose angle can be varied and fixed as required, functioning as a specialized (adjustable) type of set square.

q: 43. Set square are used to draw .............
explain: Set squares, used alone or in combination with a T-square, can draw vertical lines, inclined lines (at fixed standard angles), and parallel lines, so all of these apply.

q: 44. The purpose of making the drawing board with seasoned soft wood .............
options: for fixing of drawing paper with the help of drawing pin
explain: Seasoned soft wood is chosen for drawing boards mainly because it allows drawing pins to be easily pushed in and removed for fixing the paper, without damaging the board or the pins.

q: 45. To prevent warping of the board ............. are created at its back.
explain: Battens (cleats) are fixed across the back of a drawing board to prevent it from warping (bending) over time due to changes in humidity and temperature.

q: 46. The hardness of the pencil lead increase as numeral letter H .............
explain: In pencil grading, a higher number preceding 'H' (e.g., 4H vs 2H) indicates progressively harder, lighter graphite lead, so hardness increases as the H-number increases.

q: 47. A machine which is designed to perform the function of T-square, set square, scale and protractor is .............
explain: A drafting machine is precisely the tool that combines and replaces the functions of the T-square, set squares, scale, and protractor in one adjustable device.

q: 48. The needle point of the compass should be ............. than the lead point.
explain: The compass's steel needle point should be kept slightly shorter than the pencil lead point so the pencil tip makes full contact with the paper while the needle firmly anchors the center.

q: 49. Chisel pencils are used to draw .............
explain: A pencil sharpened to a chisel edge maintains a consistent line width when guided along a straightedge, making it best suited for drawing straight lines of uniform thickness.

q: 50. The working edge of T-square is used to .............
options: as a base of set square
explain: The T-square's working (blade) edge is used both to directly draw horizontal parallel lines and to serve as a guiding base against which a set square is placed to draw vertical/inclined lines.
